newsitem.title: USA: Clinton gets early birthday present -- end to strike.
newsitem.headline: Clinton gets early birthday present -- end to strike.

text.p: President Bill Clinton got an early present for his 51st birthday on Tuesday -- the good news that a 15-day package delivery strike appeared to be ending.

Clinton received word of a tentative deal between United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union after midnight upon returning to his vacation home after a night out with his wife Hillary and daughter Chelsea.
"I am pleased that the parties negotiated in good faith," Clinton said in a written statement read to reporters early on Tuesday by a White House spokesman shortly after the settlement was announced.

"Today's agreement represents their hard work and determination to reconcile their differences for the good of the company, its employees and the customers they serve," Clinton said. "The issues that were at the heart of their negotiations are important to our nation's economic strength, and to all Americans."
Clinton said he wanted to especially thank Labor Secretary Alexis Herman for working "tirelessly" with both sides to enable them to reach the deal.

Clinton, here on the Massachusetts island of Martha's Vineyard on a three-week vacation, spoke to Herman shortly before the deal was announced, and later was informed that a deal had been reached by presidential aide Bruce Lindsey, said White House spokesman Barry Toiv.

The president had said after his arrival here on Sunday that he had a "gut feeling" that an end to the strike was near and said he felt the Teamsters risked losing public support if the walkout dragged on. His comment was seen as exerting pressure on the union.
Now, Clinton can enjoy his birthday without worrying that a prolonged strike could endanger the U.S. economy and hurt his public approval rating, at 59 percent as high as it has ever been.
